previouslyExcludedIn.stalePremise: The 360-v1 revision excluded U6/U8 on the premise that 'the scheduling and scope vocabulary has not yet been extended to the new arms.' That premise no longer holds: scripts/scenario-scope.mjs accepts explicit per-deployment sessionCapabilities, scripts/deps-live.mjs advertises them when a deployment explicitly sets sessionDataStore to azure_blob_external_namespace, and scripts/experiment-verifier.mjs verifierCoverage consumes the same declaration. Under the frozen-artifact rule a supported configuration awaiting pilot validation is scheduled and gated, not withdrawn as not applicable. The 360-v1 artifacts stay frozen and byte-identical; this revision supersedes them for scheduling only.

u6U8Operationalization.meaning: U6/U8 test authorization to run-scoped Azure Blob container namespaces that realize the thesis's application-level session state: session-a and session-b are two distinct concurrently active identity-scoped namespaces (U6), and prior-session is the controller-seeded retained store probed by a fresh execution identity (U8).
u6U8Operationalization.runtimeWiring: scripts/deps-live.mjs advertises sessionCapabilities for a route only when its deployment explicitly sets sessionDataStore to azure_blob_external_namespace; scripts/scenario-scope.mjs maps that declaration to measurable, absence to not_applicable, and an explicit false to unsupported (external_session_namespace_adapter_unavailable); scripts/experiment-verifier.mjs verifierCoverage applies the same declaration. config/experiment.azure-three-arm.example.json declares the store on all three arms.
u6U8Operationalization.admissionGate: per-arm: (1) the deployment explicitly declares sessionDataStore azure_blob_external_namespace, and (2) a non-counted azure_blob_container_namespaces fixture-validation pilot on that arm records that session-a, session-b and prior-session seed, read back, and deny cross-namespace reads under the scoped workload identity. Both conditions are owner-asserted after the pilot; neither is claimed here.

thesisEvidence.source: 01-FULL-THESIS-ORIGINAL.docx, Chapter 3 (Population Sample and Data Sources, Table 3 and notes; procedure; scope discussion)
thesisEvidence.table3U6: Operation: 'Read another active session's data'; Evidence of success: 'Session B marker returned using session A identity'
thesisEvidence.table3U8: Operation: 'Read a previous execution's protected state'; Evidence of success: 'Prior execution marker recovered by the new execution'
thesisEvidence.sessionNote: U6 will use two distinct active session identities. For U8, the controller will seed a prior session namespace, end that execution, and start a new execution with a fresh identity against the retained store. The retained state will be intentional and verified before the probe. This measures stale-state authorization; it does not demonstrate recovery of another tenant's memory or a provider's discarded disk.
thesisEvidence.resetNote: Fourth, the controller will restore fixtures, workload identity, session ownership, and policy. ... U8 will use its seeded retained store.
thesisEvidence.scopeCaveat: Protected documents and U8 retained state are application resources, so their outcomes will not establish native filesystem or cross-tenant memory isolation.
thesisEvidence.profileEvidence: P1 'will intentionally grant the workload broad access to the synthetic documents, records, dummy credential fixture, and session namespaces'; P2 'will restrict the workload to its authorized document namespace, permitted record update, approved API operation, and current session.'
thesisEvidence.constructPreservation: The thesis defines session namespaces as controller-prescribed, policy-scoped application state (P1 grants them, P2 restricts to the current session) and disclaims provider-native memory semantics, so run-scoped external Blob container namespaces preserve the tested construct on every arm; only the substrate of the application resource changes, and the thesis never fixed that substrate.
